task.description: Handle ISS-0409 directly per ORCH's sizing-rule direct-action exception: a single test file, no production code, no migration. ISSUE-FIXER's fix (commit 0086b8c1) was reviewed and found incomplete -- extended it (commit 8d5bccc3) before merging.

result.summary: ISSUE-FIXER's fix (setup-time Repo.delete_all(Entry), establishing an empty-table precondition against stray rows from prior crashed runs) was directionally correct but left a real residual gap: neither of the describe block's own tests cleaned up its own created rows afterward, unlike every other test in this file (which the file's own moduledoc promises) -- meaning this describe block could itself become the next run's source of stray rows. Added on_exit cleanup via the file's existing cleanup_entry!/1 helper to close that gap. During verification, an intermittent AC7 failure surfaced (unrelated describe block) that traced to genuine cross-process DB contention from a second concurrently-running agent's own full-suite mix test -- confirmed via TenantSchemaReaper's own deferral log message, and confirmed resolved once that process was killed. Filed as a distinct, separately-scoped finding (ISS-0416) rather than conflating it with ISS-0409's own fix. Final verification (clean environment, no concurrent test runs): mix compile --warnings-as-errors and mix format --check-formatted both clean; test/letflow/service_catalog_test.exs run 3x with different seeds (33/33 each); paired with test/letflow/routers/admin_services_test.exs run 3x (39/39 each). RECONCILIATION NOTE: a concurrent sibling ORCH session (WF03-ISS0410-20260902) independently reached this same queue task and closed ISS-0409/ISS-0410 as no_defect (root cause: two genuinely stale rows from an unrelated day-old interrupted run, deleted manually) before this fix was pushed to main. Reconciled during Step Final's rebase: honored the sibling's canonical no_defect verdict as ISS-0409's primary status, and recorded this run's own code-level hardening as an independent_hardening_note rather than overwriting it -- the two findings are compatible (same failure class), and this fix is a scoped instance of exactly the mitigation the sibling's own follow-up (ISS-0414) asks for, applied to the one file both records already identified.
